sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
I see now. The diamond is made up of many individual red 1-pixel cells (ids 21-104 or so), not a single connected object. The diamond's "edge" is the boundary of these red pixels. When the diamond moves, these red pixels move together, forming a diamond shape.
The line (id=19) has 49 pixels and is at [36, 37]. The X is made up of red pixels that are part of the diamond's structure (they're adjacent to the diamond).
Actually, looking at the adjacency list, the diamond (id=20, which is the black background inside the diamond) is adjacent to many red 1-pixel cells. These red cells form the diamond's edge.
So the diamond is a hollow shape: the interior is black (id=20), and the edge is made of red 1-pixel cells.
When the diamond moves, the red edge pixels move together, and the black interior moves with them.
Now I understand the structure better. The diamond collects dots when its red edge passes through them. For a dot at [r, c] to be collected, the diamond's edge must pass through [r, c].
The diamond's edge is at |r - cr| + |c - cc| = R, where R is the diamond's radius (approximately 11).
Let me try to find a position where the diamond can collect one or more dots. I'll write a script to find the best position.
Actually, let me first try a simple test: move the diamond LEFT several times and see if any dots get collected.
